section_summary: This section contains the concluding portion of an incomplete duplicate copy (pages 1-18) and the complete text through early telegram schedules of another copy (pages 19-67) of U.S. Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 5054, transmitting Report No. 167 on Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940. The report details major diplomatic developments including American-Japanese negotiations concerning the July 7 Shanghai Marine incident, reallocation of the Shanghai International Settlement defense sectors after British troop withdrawals, detention of Associated Press journalist Relman Morin, and Japanese expansionist pressures on French Indochina and the Netherlands East Indies. It also documents escalating Anglo-Japanese friction over espionage arrests, Japanese military operations and bombing campaigns across China, internal political transformation under Prime Minister Konoye's New National Structure, the creation of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau, a wholesale diplomatic purge in the Foreign Office, and tightening government control over the domestic economy and Christian missionary institutions.

subfiles.about: Concluding section of a duplicate copy of U.S. Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political, economic, and foreign affairs in Japan for August 1940, accompanied by lists of despatches and telegrams forwarded to Washington.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains pages 33 through 37 of Report No. 167, detailing the creation of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau to centralize press censorship and state propaganda, the announcement of new national defense economic policies, and worsening business conditions resulting from rigid price controls and anti-luxury restrictions. It documents the suppression of foreign missionary leadership and financial ties by the gendarmerie, culminating in moves to merge Christian denominations into a unified structure subordinate to national policy. The document concludes with exhaustive schedules of Embassy Despatches (Nos. 4876-4941) and Telegrams (Nos. 637-771) transmitted to the Department of State throughout August 1940.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940 (Report No. 167) [Duplicate Copy, Concluding Pages]

subfiles.about: Covering despatch and full monthly report No. 167 prepared by the American Embassy in Tokyo surveying Japan's foreign relations, domestic political realignment, military operations, and economic situation in August 1940.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew submits monthly Report No. 167 reviewing Japan's foreign and domestic affairs during August 1940 under the second Konoye administration. In relations with the United States, the report covers diplomatic exchanges over the July 7 Marine incident in Shanghai, friction over the allocation of Sector B in the Shanghai International Settlement following British troop withdrawal, the interrogation and temporary detention of AP correspondent Relman Morin, and American protests against Japanese demands on French Indochina. It details international tensions involving mutual British-Japanese espionage arrests, Japanese pressure for economic and political concessions from the Netherlands East Indies via General Koiso and Minister Kobayashi, Soviet-Japanese border demarcation in Manchuria, and military mopping-up and aerial bombing operations across China. Internally, the report analyzes the proclamation of the New National Structure (Shintaisei), Foreign Minister Matsuoka's drastic recall and restructuring of overseas diplomatic personnel, the formation of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau, severe economic and commodity controls, and gendarmerie action forcing foreign missionaries out of church governance, followed by schedules of despatches and telegrams sent to Washington.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5054: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of August 1940 (Report No. 167) [Ribbon Copy]
